methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $2M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Ground Control Development, a seed-stage housing and construction technology company founded by Lizzy Manzi, has raised $2M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a private comparables universe of five companies operating in the same sector—BotBuilt, Apis Cor, Unlimited Industries, ADMARES, and Hedral—with no direct public market benchmarks available for triangulation.

A stage-progression methodology was applied, using the $2M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement in this sector. This approach yielded an implied valuation of $5M. Given the limited data set and single applicable method, the analysis supports a valuation range of $4M to $6M, with a median estimate of $5M.

Key uncertainties warrant noting: the analysis relies on a single triangulation method given data constraints, and the private comparables set is modest in size. The absence of public market peers limits benchmarking depth. The stage-progression method assumes typical market conditions and comparable deal velocity, which may not hold for frontier construction technology. A post-seed financing round would materially refine this estimate through disclosed terms and updated market conditions.
